name: Sheva
overview: Sheva was a male scribe who served King David, as recorded in 2 Samuel 20:25. His role as a scribe indicates a position of trust and responsibility in the administration of David's kingdom. Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Sheva is a proper name meaning 'vanity, emptiness; one who will emulate.' This meaning is noted in the Hebrew context but was not given by God. The name itself does not carry a divine mandate or special title beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Sheva beyond his role as a scribe for King David. There are no further relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sheva's significance lies in his service as a scribe during King David's reign, a role critical for maintaining official records and communications in the kingdom. While not a prominent narrative figure, his mention highlights the administrative structure supporting David's rule. His presence in the biblical record underscores the importance of faithful servants who contributed to the governance of Israel under God's anointed king.
